newsitem.title: USA: Clinton doubtful of apology to blacks for slavery.
newsitem.headline: Clinton doubtful of apology to blacks for slavery.

text.p: President Bill Clinton is not actively considering whether the United States should apologise to black Americans for enslaving their ancestors, the White House said on Tuesday.
When he launched a year-long initiative in June on ways to breach the racial divide, Clinton said he needed time to decide whether the government should formally apologise to blacks for slavery.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry gave a strong indication at his daily news briefing that an apology would not be forthcoming anytime soon, if at all.
"The president has, really, in a way, put that issue aside and said that's not going to be the focus of his race initiative," McCurry said.
A seven-member advisory board that Clinton appointed to make recommendations on ways to mend relations between the races has said it would look at the apology question, which McCurry said was proper.
But he said Clinton has had many conversations with people in the black community and that he often hears an apology is not an issue to dwell on in the race initiative.

"He's had lots of conversations with people, and very few have suggested that that's the critical issue that ought to be at the centre of this process or that it be the issue that begins the work that he intends to do," he said.

As part of his outreach to minorities, Clinton met for two hours on Tuesday evening with black leaders including Rev. Jesse Jackson and Kweisi Mfume, the president of the National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People (NAACP).

"Yes an apology is in order, a repair is in order, and a remedy is in order," Jackson, a political leader and media commentator, told reporters after the meeting. "This is much too serious to be dealt with superficially as ... rhetoric."
Mfume, in contrast, did not call for an apology, arguing that an expression of regret without concrete actions to improve the lot of black people was meaningless.
